origin: The bold, angular letters of medieval European manuscripts, called blackletter because the strokes are so dense the page looks black. The Gutenberg Bible of the 1450s was printed in it.
whenToUse: Classic logos such as tradition, beer, or newspaper mastheads.
One or two words of Latin text.
whenNotToUse: Using Unicode decorative characters as real text (problems with search and screen reading).
accessibility: Screen readers read Unicode decorative characters one by one, so add role=img and an aria-label (Weekend Market).
Write the Korean phrase alongside to convey the meaning.
Don't use decorative characters for text that must be searched or copied.
A toggle to compare with plain text shows the difference the effect makes.
